title: Stargazy Pie
subtitle: Cornish pilchard pie with fish heads emerging through the pastry
excerpt: Stargazy pie is the most distinctive-looking pie in British cooking: whole pilchards or sardines with their heads poking up through a shortcrust lid, as if gazing at the stars. It comes from the Cornish village of Mousehole and is traditionally made on Tom Bawcock's Eve. The fish heads in the pastry release their oils into the filling as the pie bakes.
sourceNotes: Stargazy pie is a Cornish dish associated with Mousehole, a small fishing village. Tom Bawcock's Eve on 23 December commemorates a fisherman who allegedly sailed out in a storm to save the village from starvation, returning with a catch of seven types of fish. The pie is traditionally made with pilchards, eggs, and bacon under a pastry lid through which the fish heads emerge.

glossaryTerms.definition: The Cornish name for a fully grown sardine (Sardina pilchardus). Historically caught in large numbers off the Cornish coast; now sold as Cornish sardines. Use fresh sardines as a direct substitute.

content.text: Stargazy pie is a dish made to eat and to look at. The presentation is intentional and unusual: the fish heads peer through holes in the pastry, a visual that is striking enough to be memorable. The traditional fish is the
. Fresh sardines are a direct substitute. The filling is a practical combination of whole oily fish, hard-boiled eggs, and bacon in a creamy sauce: satisfying as food, not just spectacle.

attrs.title: Pilchards and sardines
attrs.body: Pilchards and sardines are the same fish at different stages of maturity. Fresh Cornish sardines or large fresh sardines from a fishmonger are the right fish. You need whole fish with their heads on for the traditional presentation. Ask the fishmonger to gut and clean them but leave the heads.

items.prepNote: whole, gutted and cleaned, heads on
finely chopped and softened in butter

content.text: Fry the lardons until crisp. Mix with the softened onion, hard-boiled egg quarters, chopped parsley, double cream, lemon zest and juice, and mustard powder. Season well.
Spread the filling in the base of a pie dish. Lay the whole sardines on top with their tails in the filling and their heads pointing to the edge of the dish.

Heat the oven to 190°C fan. Roll the pastry to fit the pie dish. Lay over the top, then cut slits at the edge where each fish head is positioned and push the head gently through so it pokes up through the pastry. Brush the pastry with beaten egg. Bake for 40 to 45 minutes until golden.

items.symptom: The fish heads have fallen back into the pie during baking
items.cause: The pastry was not cut tightly enough around the neck of each fish.
items.fix: Cut a small, snug slit , just wide enough for the fish neck , so the pastry grips the head in position during baking.

items.symptom: The sardine flesh is dry and tough
items.cause: Sardines are oily fish and are easily overcooked.
items.fix: The 40 to 45 minute bake is sufficient to cook the sardines through. They cook quickly and do not need pre-cooking.

items.symptom: The filling is loose under the pastry
items.cause: The cream was too thin or the eggs were not enough to bind it.
items.fix: The filling should be thick enough to hold the sardines in position before the lid goes on. Reduce the cream slightly on the hob if it seems very liquid.

items.symptom: The pastry is wet underneath from the fish oils
items.cause: Sardines release oil during baking that has run into the pastry base.
items.fix: Stargazy pie does not have a pastry base , only a lid. The filling sits directly in the dish, and the oil is part of the flavour.

content.text: Stargazy pie is made once a year in Mousehole on 23 December, Tom Bawcock's Eve. It commemorates a fisherman who brought in a catch during a winter storm. Outside Cornwall it is mainly known by reputation: the fish-heads-through-pastry image circulates as an example of eccentric British food. It is a very good pie, not merely a curiosity. Oily fish, cured pork, egg, and cream under pastry is a complete and satisfying meal.
